nd work that stopped making progress
# dsh-notify
English | 中文
Windows 11 native toast notifications for DeepSeek Harness.

Work keeps running while you are looking at something else. A turn that is
blocked on an approval, h

as died on an error, or has quietly stopped making
progress looks exactly like a turn that is still

thinking. This plugin turns each
of those transitions into a Windows toast, and clicking a toast bri

ngs the DSH
window back to the front.
| Situation | Toast |
| A tool call waits for your approval | **DSH 需要你的授权** — the tool and its reason, with *打开 DSH* / *知

道了* buttons |
| DSH asks you a structured question | **DSH 需要你的选择** — the question header and the qu

estion itself |
| A turn or a session fails | **DSH 出错了** — the error text |
| The account needs a s

ign-in | **DSH 账号需要处理** |
| A turn that ran longer than `minRunSeconds` finishes | **DSH 已完成** — how

long it took |
| A running turn shows no progress for `stallSeconds` | **DSH 可能卡住了** — how long it
A running turn shows no progress for `stallSeconds` | **DSH 可能卡住了** — how long it has been silent |

Approvals and questions use a long-lived toast that stays in Action Center, so a
request you missed
is still there when you come back.

The copy above is the shipped default (`locale: zh`). Set `locale: en` for English
toast text; the t

able is only illustrating which events raise a toast, not a required
language.
## Shipped policy: only what needs you

The defaults interrupt you for exactly one class of event — **work that is
blocked on you**: an appr

oval, a question, an account that needs a sign-in, or a
failure. The last two rows of the table abov

e are implemented and tested but
**off by default**:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Turn both on if you would rather hear that a long turn *completed*, or that it
went quiet:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
A blocking toast can also be nudged once if nobody answers it:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The nudge re-draws the same toast with a `reminder` sound and a "仍未处理" title,
so Action Center still

holds exactly one entry for that request rather than
accumulating reminders.

If that floor is too quiet for how you work, [Recommended
configuration](#recommended-configuration)

is the smallest set of changes that closes the
gap, with the tradeoff for each one.
## What clicking a toast does

The toast body opens `openUri`, and the Desktop shell resolves that to exactly
one thing: **raising

the primary window** — restored if minimized, recreated if it
was destroyed. It does **not** navigat

e to the session that raised the toast. The
shell wires `second-instance` to a zero-argument callbac

k, so the command line
carrying the URI is discarded, and the only URI it recognises anywhere is
`ds

h://open`. A toast raised by a background or subagent session therefore brings
you back to DSH, not

st raised by a background or subagent session therefore brings
you back to DSH, not to that session.

Landing on the exact session would need the Desktop shell to accept a
session-bearing deep link. No

Host plugin can do it: the click arrives from
Windows, not from the renderer, so there is nothing fo
r a plugin to intercept.
## Why Windows PowerShell, and not PowerShell 7
The plugin probes Windows PowerShell first and only then `pwsh`, on purpose:

- **PowerShell 7** runs on .NET (Core), which dropped the built-in WinRT type
projection. `Windows.D

ata.Xml.Dom.XmlDocument` and `Windows.UI.Notifications.*`
cannot be resolved there at all, so the to

ast cannot even be built.
- **Windows PowerShell 5.1** runs on .NET Framework, whose WinRT projectio

n ships
in the box. This is the PowerShell that can post a toast.

`shell: auto` runs the probe at activation and logs which one won. Point
`shell:` at an absolute `pw

sh.exe` or `powershell.exe` to choose explicitly; a
probe that fails leaves the plugin inert with a

logged reason rather than a
silently broken notifier.
## What counts as progress

Only relevant while `notifyOnStall` is on. The watchdog treats four things as proof that
a turn is a

live: live assistant tokens (`agent/assistant-stream`), committed session
events (`session/event`),

status transitions, and an **outstanding tool call**. The last
one is counted from the `tool/call` a

nd `tool/result` records in the session log, and it
is what stops a ten-minute command from looking

stuck: while a call is in flight the hint
is suppressed entirely, and any `step/end` or `turn/end` r

esets the count so an
interrupted call cannot silence the hint forever.

The wording is still *no observable progress* rather than a failure, and a model wait
longer than `s

tallSeconds` still triggers it — raise `stallSeconds` above your longest
legitimate model wait.
## Why is it not notifying?

The failure mode of a notification plugin is silence, so activation is traced to
`%TEMP%\dsh-notify-

trace.log` (`$TMPDIR` elsewhere). The trace is bounded, synchronous,
and cannot throw into the plugi

ace.log` (`$TMPDIR` elsewhere). The trace is bounded, synchronous,
and cannot throw into the plugin.

Two listeners observe **waterfalls** (`approval/request`, `user-questions/request`)
because those ar

e the only signals those services publish — neither emits a companion
event. A waterfall ends the mo

ment any listener *claims* the request by returning an
answer instead of calling `next()`, and the a

nswering listener is the browser UI,
registered through `ctx.remote.$on` when a page connects. An ob

server appended after it
therefore never runs, which looks exactly like a plugin that is active and

appended after it
therefore never runs, which looks exactly like a plugin that is active and quiet.

Both observers are registered with `prepend` for that reason. Do not remove it: the
notification mus

t not depend on which listener answers or on when a page happened to
connect. The trace records ever

y listener entry, and `agent/status` — an emit event no
listener can claim — is traced as a control,

so "dispatch never arrives" stays
distinguishable from "this chain terminated early".
| Last trace line | Meaning |

| none at all | the module never activated |
| stops before `apply finished` | activation stopped pa

rt-way; the last line names the milestone |
